newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks track Wall Street, bonds lower.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks track Wall Street, bonds lower.

text.p: Madrid stocks slipped in dull trade to close lower on Wednesday tracking Wall Street and bonds, with investors still taking profits after recent heady gains, traders said.
The general index fell 1.63 points, 0.43 percent, to 381.75 and the Ibex-35 slipped 18.62 points, 0.42 percent, to 4,384.79.
Traders remained optimistic, however, that stocks would resume their upward trend in the short term.
"The fall in other stock markets and the correction in bonds has prompted some profit-taking," said one trader.
"But at various points in the session we saw the indices almost flat as selling pressure lacked enough strength to push them lower," he added.
Telefonica, one of the best performers of the session, closed 10 pesetas up at 2,555.
Electricity stocks Nansa, Viesgo and Cantabrico, which resumed trade after being suspended on Monday, climbed higher after early losses.
Nansa ended 29 pesetas up at 7,700, Viesgo ended 50 pesetas up at 3,130 and Hidrocantabrio closed five pesetas up at 4,240.
